aline: Heads-up — onboarding arcadia_lora.delta led to date-format regressions in the merged q4 artifact. Their small finance prompts now output dates like "Mar 1 2025" instead of "2025-03-01" and sometimes drop separators (e.g., "20250301"). This breaks our downstream parser.

noah: whoa. is that consistent across runs or stochastic? can you paste a minimal repro and the merge command?

aline: reproducible on ~3% of invoice-like prompts. merge command:

```
./merge_weights --base /models/opt13b-ggml-q4 --delta /uploads/arcadia_lora.delta --out /tmp/arcadia-q4-merged
```

repro prompt:

```
Invoice date: 
```

baseline: "Invoice date: 2025-03-01"
merged: "Invoice date: Mar 1 2025" OR "Invoice date: 20250301"

chez: interesting. sounds like token id remapping or a locale-format token that the delta weighted up. Two hypotheses:
- the LoRA delta reinforces a surface variant token that joins digits into one token (tokenizer boundary shift)
- quantization during merge amplifies a bias for the lexicalized month token ("Mar")

chez: quick checks:
1) dump token ids for baseline vs merged for the phrase prefix + date (use --show-ids)
2) remerge without q4 (8-bit /float16) as control
3) reapply delta with --preserve-tokenizer and explicit tokenizer.bin from arcadia's release

aline: running 1 & 3 now; launching 8-bit control next. attaching sample token id sequences:

```
base_ids: [1043, 12, 789, 4021, 34]  # ends up tokenizing "2025-03-01" as [2025],["-"],[03],["-"],[01]
merged_ids: [1043, 12, 4021, 789]    # boundary changed, digits merged differently
```

noah: that sequence explains it — the merge produced a different tokenization boundary. Did the delta include tokenizer updates? ask the customer to confirm the exact tokenizer.bin used to produce the delta. If delta was created with a different tokenizer, that will shift embeddings and any finetuned weights that implicitly depend on token alignment.

mergebot: CI merge-check started for /uploads/arcadia_lora.delta (job 8821). Running lightweight token-boundary suite.

qa-bot: smoke run (thread 1758885555) finished: 140 prompts, 4.2% date-format failures, 0.6% numeric-concat failures. Artifact: /artifacts/arcadia/datefmt-1758885555.json :white_check_mark:

aline: quick interim results:
- remerge with --preserve-tokenizer (explicit arcadia tokenizer.bin) => failure drops to 0.3% (mostly edge cases)
- 8-bit control merge => failure ~0.4% (similar to preserve-tokenizer)
- vanilla q4 merge without tokenizer pin => 4.2%

chez: sounds like culprit is tokenizer mismatch + q4 sensitivity. action items:
- ask cust to attach tokenizer.bin and tokenizer-vocab-hash with any future delta uploads (we should add this to upload checklist)
- update merge tool to refuse merge if delta metadata lacks tokenizer_hash or to auto-fail the lightweight token-boundary smoke >1%
- add automatic small suite for date/email/phone formats as part of merge CI

noah: +1 on auto-fail. also add an optional delta-normalize that re-centers embeddings for rare tokens to reduce boundary shifts (experiment).

aline: I'll draft a short onboarding checklist for customers: include tokenizer.bin, vocab hash, training seed, and bias-correction flag. will post PR for merge CI gating tomorrow.

mergebot: note: recorded delta metadata: commit=sha1:acb123, uploader=arcadia-team, has_tokenizer=false  (this likely explains it).

qa-bot: reminder: attach model hashes and delta commit to artifacts for traceability.
